result.instructions:
cua-driver: background GUI automation. No shell: for non-GUI outcomes use an app API/SDK, CLI or filesystem and read the result back there.

1. `list_windows({app:"Name"})` or `launch_app` for `pid` and `window_id`.
2. Read narrowly: `get_window_state` with `query:"Save"`. Re-read with `since:"latest"`.
3. Act by `element_token` (AT-SPI): row `[N]` is `<snapshot_id>:N`. Pixels only for surfaces missing from the tree.
4. Act through `run_steps({steps:[{tool,args}],observe:{}})`, even for one step: stops at the first failure, returns what changed. Loops, branches or retries: one `run_script` call.
5. Verify at checkpoints, not after every action: `verify_state(pid, window_id, expect)`. `unknown` and `effect:"unverifiable"` are not success.

Use the narrowest semantic route first: `set_window_frame` plus `list_windows` for geometry, typed browser tools for pages. Stay in the background; `delivery_mode:"foreground"` only if refused or unverifiable.

Chrome/Edge/Brave page: `get_browser_state({pid, window_id})`, its `detail.next_call` (`browser_prepare`) if refused, then `browser_click`/`browser_type`/`browser_pointer` (hover, drag); never desktop pointer tools.

`start_session` is optional; repeat a short `session` label on every call that accepts it. On continuation/recent-work, call `history_status`; if ready, make one bounded initial `history_query` before broad discovery.

Guides: `get_guide({topic})` (drag, browser, permissions, batching, menus), `skill://cua-driver/SKILL.md`, LINUX.md (X11/Wayland status, AT-SPI bus, BETA-level support).

[gui-gate] Actions go through a value gate before they run. Usually they execute at once. If a call returns a message starting with "[gate]", nothing was executed: do exactly what it says (re-read, re-aim with a screenshot, take the safe way it names, or ask the user and retry with gate_confirm). The gate settles doubtful and risky steps itself (rules, the user's own words, its own independent reviewer, or a person); it never asks you to approve your own action. To save time the gate omits the screenshot from get_window_state when the element tree is enough; pass include_screenshot:true when you really need pixels. Each action's result already carries a fresh read of the window: do not read it again before the next step. Several steps whose targets you can already see go in ONE run_actions call. If the user's request is known, pass it verbatim once with gate_task. When the gate refuses a risky step it tells you a safe way to go on: take it and finish the task.

tools.description:
List Linux apps — both currently running and installed-but-not-running — with per-app state flags:

- running: is a process for this app live? (pid is 0 when false)
- active: reserved (Linux X11/Wayland focus model differs from frontmost-app); always false.
- kind: `"desktop"` for XDG `.desktop` launcher entries.
- launch_path: the launcher command from `Exec=` (field codes stripped). Pass to `launch_app(launch_path=...)`.

all.description: Also list kernel threads and system daemons (hidden by default).

tools.name: list_apps

tools.description: List top-level windows. Each record includes z_index (integer or null; higher values are closer to the front; null means stacking order is unavailable and callers must not infer one). To select a frontmost candidate, take the maximum integer z_index; if every value is null, use an explicit fallback instead of relying on array order. Filter with `app` or `pid`: an unfiltered call lists every window on the host.

app.description: Only windows of apps whose name contains this text (case-insensitive), or whose bundle id equals it.

on_screen_only.description: When true, filter to visible windows only. Default false.

pid.description: Only list windows owned by this process ID.

tools.name: list_windows

z_index.description: Higher values are closer to the front. Null means the provider cannot observe stacking order; callers must not infer an order from array position or treat null as zero.

tools.description: Walk a running app's AT-SPI tree and return it ONCE, as compact Markdown by default (`tree_format:"markdown"`). Every actionable element is tagged `[N]` (an element_index); its element_token is `<snapshot_id>:N`, where `snapshot_id` is printed in the response header and returned in structuredContent. Pass `tree_format:"elements"` for the structured `elements` array instead (explicit `element_token`, `role`, `label`, `value`, `enabled`, `selected`, `actions`, `frame: {x,y,w,h}` when AT-SPI reports usable bounds, `parent_index`, `depth`), or `"both"` for both (about twice the size).

include_accessibility_tree.description: Default true — walk the AT-SPI tree and return it (per `tree_format`) alongside the screenshot.

include_screenshot.description: Default true — returns a grounding screenshot alongside the tree.

max_depth.description: Cap on the AT-SPI tree walk depth. Omit for the default (uncapped). Lower for deeply nested apps.

max_dimension.description: Legacy optional cap on the returned screenshot's long edge.

max_elements.description: Cap on total AT-SPI nodes walked. Default 250 (5 000 with full_output:true); the response states when the tree was cut.

pid.description: Process ID that owns the window.

tools.description: Launch a Linux app in the background. Provide launch_path (preferred — round-trip the value from list_apps), name (tried as a direct command, then matched against installed .desktop applications, then handed to xdg-open if it is a URL or existing file path), bundle_id (ignored on Linux), or urls (list of URLs to open). Resolution precedence: launch_path > name > bundle_id. Errors when the name resolves to nothing launchable.

tools.name: launch_app

tools.description: Persistently activate a window so subsequent input lands on it. This deliberately breaks the no-foreground contract and is not part of the normal input ladder. For an ordinary `background_unavailable` response, retry only the refused action with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`; the input tool performs its own activate, act, and restore sequence. Use `bring_to_front` only for a focus-proxy surface that must remain foreground across multiple calls, such as a remote desktop session, or when repeated action-scoped activation prevents the remote surface from accepting input.

pid.description: Process ID of the app to activate.

window_id.description: X11 window id (xid) to activate. If omitted, the first window of `pid` is used.

tools.name: bring_to_front

tools.description: Resolve an exact application-menu path one live native level at a time and invoke its final item through accessibility APIs. Missing, ambiguous, disabled, or structurally mismatched segments fail closed; this tool never falls back to pixels. Menu paths and refusals: `get_guide({topic:"menus"})`.

inputSchema.description:
Exact, immediate-child application menu path to resolve and invoke through
the operating system's accessibility API. Path labels are matched after
trimming surrounding whitespace and otherwise remain case-sensitive. On
macOS, three periods in a label also match the ellipsis character that
native menu titles use (`Save As...` finds `Save As…`).

path.description:
Menu labels from the top-level menu to the item, e.g. `["File", "Save As..."]`
(1 to 16 labels).

pid.description: Process ID of the application that owns the menu.

window_id.description: Window ID from list_windows whose menu is invoked.

tools.description:
Click against a target pid. **Prefer `element_token` over pixel coordinates** — element_token works on backgrounded / hidden windows, surfaces a stable handle, and tells you what you're clicking via the cached AT-SPI element's role + label. Reach for `x, y` only when the target is a canvas / custom-drawn surface that doesn't appear in the AT-SPI tree.

Provide either (window_id + x/y) or (pid + element_token).

tools.name: scroll
request_human
tools.description: Ask the person at this computer. kind=approve: a yes/no on what you are about to do. kind=answer: a short free-text answer (e.g. which option they want). kind=takeover: ask them to do a step themselves (log in, solve a captcha, anything you cannot or should not do); it returns when they are done. Use only when a person is really needed.

question.description: What you need from them, in one or two plain sentences.

tools.name: gate_task
tools.description: Tell the gate the user's request, VERBATIM, once at the start (copy their words; do not summarise or add to them). The gate lets a risky step through without stopping you when the request explicitly asks for it (e.g. "overwrite report.pdf"). It can be set only once.

request.description: The user's request, word for word.

tools.name: gate_report
tools.description: Value-gate statistics for this session: how many actions ran directly, how many observations/screenshots were requested or avoided, interventions by type, and gate overhead.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run a bash command (or a short script) on this computer and get its exit code and output. Use it for terminal, file and document work done in code instead of by clicking: inspect files (ls, cat, head), edit spreadsheets / documents with python3 (openpyxl, odfpy, python-docx, python-pptx when installed), convert with `soffice --headless -env:UserInstallation=file:///tmp/gui-gate-lo-4053 --convert-to FMT --outdir DIR FILE` (the -env part lets it run while LibreOffice is open). Every command is checked by the gate like a typed terminal command (overwrites, moves, deletes, permission changes and other risky effects need the user's words, the gate's reviewer or a person). If you change a file that is open in an app, reload it there (LibreOffice: File > Reload) or the app's own save will write its old copy over your change. No interactive programs (no editors, pagers or password prompts): stdin is empty.

command.description: bash command line or script (heredocs allowed)

timeout_s.description: seconds before the command is killed (default 30, max 300)

tools.name: check_done
tools.description: Before you reply DONE, call this once: the gate gathers evidence about the end state (files the task names: exist? changed during this session?; files changed this session; unsaved-document markers; visible Calc cells; terminal tail; open windows; steps the gate refused; your plan's open milestones) and lists possible gaps. It does not judge the task; you decide whether to finish or fix something first.

files.description: extra paths you produced or changed (optional)

tools.name: set_plan
tools.description: Your own plan, kept by the gate (no model involved). Call it once at the start with 2-6 short milestones and your feasibility verdict: feasible:false when the task cannot be done on this computer (the app has no such feature or setting, the thing asked for does not exist, the file or data is not there) - then reply FAIL with the reason instead of trying. Later calls mark milestones done (done: [numbers]) or replace the list. Every action result then ends with a one-line progress note, and check_done lists milestones still open.

feasible.description: false = this task cannot be done here

tools.name: run_actions
tools.description:
Batch mode: run several GUI steps in ONE call (single-step tools remain available). Each GUI step is checked by the gate like a single call. Steps, in order:
  {tool, args, expect?}  a GUI action (click, type_text, press_key, hotkey, scroll, set_value, ...) or a run_command (its output comes back in the result; a failing command stops the batch). Name things that appear only after an earlier step with args.target = {label, role?}; the gate finds them on screen when the step runs. x/y only in the first GUI step.
  {find: SELECTOR, as: "rows", max?: 20}  read the screen now and keep the matching elements.
  {for_each: "rows", do: [steps]}  repeat steps per element; inside, args.target = "$item" points at it and "$item.label" in any string is its label.
  {if: {exists: SELECTOR} | {not_exists: SELECTOR}, then: [steps], else?: [steps]}
  {read: SELECTOR, as?: "name"}  report the matching elements' labels/values in the result.
SELECTOR = {label} exact, {label_contains}, {label_regex} and/or {role}. The batch stops at the first refused or failed step, when a dialog opens unexpectedly (a popup menu is fine), or when an expect fails ({title_contains} or {new_window: true}). You get what ran plus one fresh read of the window at the end. Max 20 GUI actions.

pid.description: Default pid for steps that omit it.

window_id.description: Default window_id for steps that omit it.

steps.description: The program, see the tool description.
